scope: Theorem 10.5 (The geometry of the minimal type) of the manuscript “Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes” (preprints/Eventual-Categoricity-for-Abstract-Elementary-Classes-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 240 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dcb7401285f5ac78), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 80-81. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: On P(M), for every M0 ≤K M of size at least λ0, the preceding finite independence is the independence relation of a finitary pregeometry. Its closure, denoted by clM , has the following properties. 1. For finite F ⊆ P(M) and any maximal independent S ⊆ F, the set clM (F) consists exactly of those points that do not independently extend S. Equivalently, clM (F) is the set of points forced by F. 2. Strong embeddings over M0 preserve and reflect finite closure. If M0 ≤K A ≤K M, then P(A) is relatively closed in P(M). 3. For finite F, | clM (F)| ≤ λ0. For every infinite F ⊆ P(M), | clM (F)| ≤ |F| + λ0. 80 In particular bases exist, all bases have the same cardinality, and each point of the span of a basis has finite basis support.
